questions.q: If $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=x-5$, find the domain of $(f\circ g)(x)$.
questions.answer: $(f\circ g)(x)=\sqrt{x-5}$, which requires $x-5\geq0$, so the domain is $x\geq5$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=x^2-1$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{1}{x}$, find $(f\circ g)(x)$ and simplify.
Find the inverse of $f(x)=x^2$ for $x\geq0$, and explain why the restriction is necessary.
questions.answer: $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x}$. The restriction $x\geq0$ is necessary because $f(x)=x^2$ is not one-to-one over all real numbers (e.g. $f(2)=f(-2)=4$), so it has no inverse function unless the domain is restricted to make it one-to-one.

questions.q: Describe the end behavior of $f(x)=-2x^4+3x^2-1$, as $x\to\infty$ and $x\to-\infty$.
questions.answer: Since the leading term is $-2x^4$ (even degree, negative coefficient), both ends of the graph point downward: as $x\to\infty$, $f(x)\to-\infty$; as $x\to-\infty$, $f(x)\to-\infty$.
Since the leading term is $3x^5$ (odd degree, positive coefficient): as $x\to\infty$, $g(x)\to\infty$; as $x\to-\infty$, $g(x)\to-\infty$.

questions.q: Find the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-3}$.
questions.answer: Vertical asymptote: where the denominator is zero: $x=3$. Horizontal asymptote: since numerator and denominator have the same degree, the asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients: $y=\dfrac{2}{1}=2$.

questions.q: Find the hole (removable discontinuity) in the graph of $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-4}{x-2}$.
questions.answer: Factor: $f(x)=\dfrac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x-2}=x+2$ for $x\neq2$. There is a hole at $x=2$, at the point $(2,4)$ (found by substituting $x=2$ into the simplified expression $x+2$).

questions.q: Simplify $\log_3(9)+\log_3(27)$, using the product rule for logarithms.

questions.answer: Combine logs: $\ln[x(x-3)]=\ln(10)$, so $x(x-3)=10$, giving $x^2-3x-10=0$. Factor: $(x-5)(x+2)=0$, so $x=5$ or $x=-2$. Since $\ln(x)$ requires $x>0$, reject $x=-2$. Solution: $x=5$.

sections.heading: Even, odd, and periodic function classification

questions.q: Determine whether $f(x)=x^4-3x^2$ is even, odd, or neither.
A function is defined as $f(x)=3x+1$ for $x<2$ and $f(x)=kx-3$ for $x\geq2$. Find the value of $k$ that makes $f$ continuous at $x=2$.
questions.answer: For continuity, the two pieces must agree at $x=2$: $3(2)+1=k(2)-3$, so $7=2k-3$, giving $2k=10$, $k=5$.

sections.heading: A multi-part function transformation and composition problem

questions.q: This question has two parts. Given $f(x)=2x-3$ and $g(x)=x^2$. (a) Find $(f\circ g)(x)$ and $(g\circ f)(x)$, in simplified form. (b) Find the value of $x$ for which $(f\circ g)(x)=(g\circ f)(x)$.
questions.answer: (a) $(f\circ g)(x)=f(x^2)=2x^2-3$. $(g\circ f)(x)=g(2x-3)=(2x-3)^2=4x^2-12x+9$. (b) Set equal: $2x^2-3=4x^2-12x+9$, so $0=2x^2-12x+12$, giving $x^2-6x+6=0$. Using the quadratic formula: $x=\dfrac{6\pm\sqrt{36-24}}{2}=\dfrac{6\pm\sqrt{12}}{2}=3\pm\sqrt{3}$.

sections.heading: Finding zeros of higher-degree functions graphically and algebraically

questions.q: A quartic function $f(x)=x^4-5x^2+4$ can be treated as a quadratic in $x^2$. Find all real zeros.
questions.answer: Let $u=x^2$: $u^2-5u+4=0$, factoring to $(u-1)(u-4)=0$, so $u=1$ or $u=4$. Since $u=x^2$: $x^2=1$ gives $x=\pm1$; $x^2=4$ gives $x=\pm2$. All real zeros: $x=-2,-1,1,2$.

sections.heading: Function operations: sum, difference, product, quotient
Symmetry and transformations of rational functions

questions.q: Explain why $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x}$ is symmetric about the origin, and state whether it is even, odd, or neither.
questions.answer: $f(-x)=\dfrac{1}{-x}=-\dfrac{1}{x}=-f(x)$. Since $f(-x)=-f(x)$, the function is odd, meaning its graph has point symmetry about the origin — rotating the graph $180^\circ$ about the origin maps it onto itself.

sections.heading: Finding a function's formula from a description of transformations

questions.q: The graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ is shifted 2 units right, stretched vertically by a factor of 3, and shifted 1 unit down. Write the equation of the resulting function.
questions.answer: Shifting right by 2 replaces $x$ with $x-2$: $\sqrt{x-2}$. Vertical stretch by 3: $3\sqrt{x-2}$. Shift down 1: $y=3\sqrt{x-2}-1$.

sections.heading: A multi-part rational function analysis problem

questions.q: This question has three parts. A function is given by $f(x)=\dfrac{2x^2-8}{x^2-x-6}$. (a) Factor the numerator and denominator completely. (b) Identify any holes and vertical asymptotes. (c) State the horizontal asymptote.
questions.answer: (a) Numerator: $2x^2-8=2(x^2-4)=2(x-2)(x+2)$. Denominator: $x^2-x-6=(x-3)(x+2)$. (b) The factor $(x+2)$ cancels, indicating a hole at $x=-2$ (specifically at the point found by substituting into the simplified expression). The remaining denominator factor $(x-3)$ gives a vertical asymptote at $x=3$ (not canceled). (c) Since the numerator and denominator have the same degree (both degree 2), the horizontal asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients: $y=\dfrac{2}{1}=2$.

questions.q: A quadratic function $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$ has $f(0)=5$, $f(1)=10$, and $f(2)=19$. Find $a$, $b$, and $c$.

sections.heading: Determining if a function has an inverse using the horizontal line test

questions.q: Explain the horizontal line test, and use it to determine whether $f(x)=x^3$ has an inverse function.
questions.answer: The horizontal line test states that a function has an inverse (is one-to-one) if and only if no horizontal line intersects its graph more than once. For $f(x)=x^3$, every horizontal line $y=k$ intersects the graph exactly once (since every real number has exactly one real cube root), so $f(x)=x^3$ does have an inverse function, namely $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}$.
